newsitem.title: USA: Shaman in pact with Merck unit.
newsitem.headline: Shaman in pact with Merck unit.

text.p: Shaman Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Wednesday it had entered into a five-year pact with Lipha S.A., a subsidiary of the German pharmaceuticals group Merck KGaA, to develop new antidiabetic drugs.
In exchange for development and marketing rights to Shaman antidiabetic drugs, Lipha will provide equity investments of $19.5 million over five years, Shaman said.

Complete funding depends on the initiation of human clinical trials of at least one compound within two years. Additional milestone payments of more than $10 million per compound are payable for each antidiabetic drug that is developed and commercialized, Shaman said.
Shaman will also receive royalties on sales outside the United States and has the right to co-promote antidiabetic products in the U.S., the company said.
Shaman develops pharmaceutical products by isolating active compounds from tropical plants that have a history of medicinal use.
